title: Voges-Proskauer (VP) Test
principle: Tests for the butanediol fermentation pathway, which produces acetoin (acetylmethylcarbinol) as an intermediate. In the presence of alpha-naphthol and potassium hydroxide (Barritt's reagent), acetoin is oxidized to diacetyl, which reacts with peptone components to form a red/pink color.
purpose: Part of the IMViC panel; identifies organisms using the butanediol fermentation pathway (e.g. Enterobacter, Klebsiella species) as opposed to the mixed-acid pathway detected by the Methyl Red test.
reagents: Barritt's reagent: alpha-naphthol solution and 40% potassium hydroxide

procedure.instruction: Inoculate MR-VP broth with the test organism and incubate for the appropriate duration.
Add alpha-naphthol solution followed by 40% potassium hydroxide to the broth (ratios and order specified by the specific reagent kit/protocol in use).
Shake gently to aerate and observe over roughly the next 15–30 minutes for a color change, since the reaction requires atmospheric oxygen and takes time to develop.

positiveResult: Development of a red/pink color, typically within the reading window specified by the reagent protocol.
negativeResult: No color change, or a copper color that is not considered a true positive by most protocols.
interpretation: Read together with the Methyl Red result from the same organism/pathway question — see the Methyl Red test entry.
precautions: Shake/aerate after adding reagents — the color-forming reaction requires oxygen.
Read within the specified window; a delayed or absent color change beyond that window is not scored positive.
limitations: A weak, ambiguous color response can occur and may need repeating with a fresh culture.
